q: The first Surah of the Glorious Qur'an is known as _____.
explanation: Suratul-Fatihah is the opening chapter of the Qur'an and is recited in every unit of the Muslim prayer.

q: The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) over a period of approximately _____ years.
explanation: The revelation began when the Prophet was 40 years old and ended shortly before his death at 63, totaling 23 years.

q: The primary source of Islamic Law (Shari'ah) is the _____.
explanation: The Qur'an is the ultimate and most authoritative source of guidance in Islam, providing the foundational principles of faith and law.

q: The 'Year of Elephant' (Amul-Fil) is significant because it was the year _____.
explanation: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) was born in 570 CE, the year Abrahah Al-Ashram attempted to destroy the Ka'bah with an army of elephants.

q: The term 'Tawhid' in Islam refers to the _____.
explanation: Tawhid is the core concept of monotheism in Islam, asserting that Allah is one and unique in His essence and attributes.

q: Which of the following is NOT among the 'As-Sihah as-Sittah' (The Six Authentic Books of Hadith)?
explanation: Muwatta Malik is a highly respected legal and Hadith collection but is not traditionally numbered among the 'Six Books'.

q: The first Caliph in Islam was _____.
explanation: Abu Bakr As-Siddiq was the first of the four Rightly Guided Caliphs, serving from 632 to 634 CE.

q: The ritual of 'Sa'y' during Hajj involves walking between the hills of _____.
explanation: Sa'y commemorates Hajar's (AS) search for water for her son Ismail (AS) between the hills of Safa and Marwa.

q: The amount of Zakat payable on wealth (gold/cash) that has reached the Nisab is _____.
explanation: Zakat on liquid assets is calculated at 2.5% (one-fortieth) of the total savings held for a full lunar year.

q: The Surah that is equivalent to one-third of the Qur'an in terms of reward is _____.
explanation: Suratul-Ikhlas summarizes the concept of Tawhid, which represents one-third of the message of the Qur'an.

q: In Islamic Inheritance (Mirath), a daughter's share when she is the only child is _____.
explanation: According to Suratan-Nisa (Q4:11), if there is only one daughter and no son, she receives half of the estate.

q: The companion known as 'Dhul-Nurayn' (The possessor of two lights) was _____.
explanation: Uthman b. Affan was given this title because he married two of the Prophet's daughters, Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum.

q: The battle in which the Muslims suffered a setback due to the disobedience of the archers was the Battle of _____.
explanation: At Uhud, the archers left their positions on the hill against the Prophet's orders, allowing the enemy to launch a counter-attack.

q: The science of the rules governing the correct pronunciation of the Qur'an is called _____.
explanation: Tajwid is the science of reciting the Qur'an according to the established rules of articulation and phonetics.

q: The angel responsible for blowing the trumpet (Sur) to signal the Day of Judgment is _____.
explanation: Israfil is the angel tasked with blowing the trumpet twice: once to end life and once to initiate the resurrection.

q: The collection and compilation of the Qur'an into a single volume was initiated during the Caliphate of _____.
explanation: Following the Battle of Yamamah, Abu Bakr ordered Zaid b. Thabit to compile the Qur'an into a single Mushaf.

q: A 'Mahr' in an Islamic marriage is the _____.
explanation: Mahr is the mandatory dowry or gift paid by the groom to the bride at the time of marriage as a sign of respect and security.

q: The act of 'Tayammum' is performed when _____ is unavailable.
explanation: Tayammum is dry ablution using clean earth/sand when water is not available or its use is harmful.

content: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) said: 'None of you truly believes until he wishes for his brother what he wishes for himself.' (Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim)

questions.q: The central theme of this Hadith is _____.
questions.explanation: The Hadith emphasizes that true faith involves selfless love and wishing good for others.
While it refers primarily to brothers in faith, Islamic ethics extend this spirit of kindness to all humanity.

q: The 'Nisab' of cattle (cows) for Zakat starts at _____ animals.
explanation: Zakat is not due on cows until the owner possesses 30, at which point one one-year-old calf (Tabi') must be given.

q: The term 'Shirk' means _____.
explanation: Shirk is the opposite of Tawhid and is considered the gravest sin in Islam as it denies the absolute Oneness of God.

q: The 'Hijrah' calendar begins from the year the Prophet (SAW) migrated from _____ to _____.
explanation: The Islamic era (Hijri) marks the migration to Madinah in 622 CE, which led to the establishment of the first Islamic state.

q: The 'Khulafah ar-Rashidun' refers to the _____.
explanation: This title is given to the first four Caliphs: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali, who followed the Sunnah of the Prophet closely.

q: The pre-Islamic period of ignorance in Arabia is known as _____.
explanation: Jahiliyyah refers to the state of affairs in Arabia before the mission of Prophet Muhammad (SAW).

q: The 'Iddah' period for a divorced woman who is not pregnant is _____.
explanation: The Qur'an specifies three monthly cycles (Quru') for a divorced woman to ensure the womb is clear before remarriage.

q: The first Mu'adhin (caller to prayer) in Islam was _____.
explanation: Bilal b. Rabah, an Abyssinian companion, was chosen by the Prophet for his strong and beautiful voice.

q: The 'Night of Power' (Laylatul-Qadr) is better than _____ months.
explanation: Suratul-Qadr states that worship on this night in Ramadan is better than a thousand months of worship.

q: The legal ruling that is 'highly recommended' but not strictly obligatory is called _____.
explanation: Mustahabb actions are rewarded if performed but do not incur punishment if omitted.

q: The Islamic concept of 'Ihsan' means _____.
opts: to worship Allah as if you see Him
explanation: Defined in the Hadith of Jibril, Ihsan is the perfection of faith where one acts with constant awareness of Allah's presence.

q: Which Caliph oversaw the expansion of Islam into Persia and Egypt?
explanation: Umar (RA) was the great administrator and conqueror under whose rule the Islamic empire expanded most rapidly.

q: The 'Sunnah' refers to the _____ of the Prophet Muhammad (SAW).
explanation: Sunnah encompasses everything the Prophet said, did, or tacitly approved (Taqrir).

q: The major theme of the 'Makkan' Surahs is usually _____.
explanation: Makkan Surahs focus on establishing faith and the oneness of Allah, while Madinan Surahs focus on law and community.

q: The 'Battle of the Trench' is also known as the Battle of _____.
explanation: It is called Al-Ahzab (The Confederates) because multiple tribes joined the Quraysh to attack Madinah.

q: The prophet mentioned most frequently by name in the Qur'an is _____.
explanation: Prophet Musa (AS) is mentioned 136 times in the Qur'an.

q: The direction (Qiblah) Muslims face during prayer was changed from _____ to Makkah.
explanation: Initially, Muslims faced Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem before the revelation changed it to the Ka'bah.

q: The 'Haram' months in which fighting is prohibited are _____.
explanation: These four months are sacred in Islam, and starting warfare during them is forbidden.

q: The act of 'Istighfar' means _____.
explanation: Istighfar is the act of saying 'Astaghfirullah' (I seek forgiveness from Allah).

q: A person who memorizes the entire Qur'an is called a _____.
explanation: Hafiz (Guardian) is the title for someone who has committed the 6,236 verses of the Qur'an to memory.

q: The 'Riddah' wars were fought during the Caliphate of Abu Bakr against _____.
explanation: After the Prophet's death, some tribes rebelled or followed false prophets; Abu Bakr fought to maintain Islamic unity.

q: The 'Al-Faruq' was the title of which Caliph?
explanation: Umar was called Al-Faruq (The one who distinguishes between truth and falsehood) for his strict justice.

q: Islamic monotheism is divided into categories: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah, Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah, and _____.
explanation: The third category involves the belief in Allah's unique Names and Attributes.

q: The 'Sujud as-Sahw' is performed when a person _____.
explanation: Two extra prostrations are performed at the end of Salat to compensate for forgetfulness or errors.

q: The primary objective of 'Sawm' (fasting) as stated in the Qur'an is _____.
explanation: Qur'an 2:183 states that fasting is prescribed so that you may achieve Taqwa (God-consciousness).

q: In Shari'ah, the prohibited acts are known as _____.
explanation: Haram refers to anything explicitly forbidden by Allah and His Messenger.

q: The first revelation came to the Prophet in the Cave of _____.
explanation: The Archangel Jibril first appeared to the Prophet in the Cave of Hira on Mount Nur.

q: Which Caliph was known for compiling the standard version of the Qur'an?
explanation: Uthman (RA) ordered the standardization of the Qur'anic text to ensure uniformity across the expanding empire.

q: The 'Asadullah' (Lion of Allah) was a title of _____.
explanation: Hamzah, the Prophet's uncle, was given this title for his extraordinary bravery in battle.

q: A 'Mushrik' is a person who _____.
explanation: The term comes from Shirk, meaning the act of attributing Allah's powers or divinity to others.

q: The five daily prayers are: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and _____.
explanation: Isha is the night prayer, the last of the five obligatory daily prayers.

q: The term 'Tafsir' refers to _____.
explanation: Tafsir is the academic study and commentary used to explain the meanings of the Qur'anic verses.

q: A Hadith narrated by only one person at every stage of the chain is called _____.
explanation: Gharib means 'solitary' or 'strange' in the science of Hadith terminology.

q: The Prophet Muhammad (SAW) belonged to the tribe of _____.
explanation: He was from the Banu Hashim clan of the noble Quraysh tribe in Makkah.

q: The 'Kharaj' in Islamic taxation refers to _____.
explanation: Kharaj is a tax levied on agricultural land in territory conquered by Muslims.

q: The Surah that describes the short duration of time and importance of faith is _____.
explanation: Suratul-Asr declares that all mankind is in loss except those with faith, good deeds, and who encourage truth and patience.

q: Which of the following is the 'Prophet of Allah' who was swallowed by a whale?
explanation: Prophet Yunus (AS) was swallowed by a whale and remained in its belly until he was released through prayer and repentance.

q: The 'Nisab' for sheep and goats for Zakat starts at _____ animals.
explanation: One must own at least 40 sheep or goats for one full lunar year before Zakat becomes due on them.

q: The 'Takbirat al-Ihram' is the _____.
explanation: This Takbir signals the formal entry into the state of prayer, during which ordinary talk and eating are forbidden.

q: The treaty signed between the Muslims and the Quraysh in 628 CE was the Treaty of _____.
explanation: Hudaibiyyah was a peace treaty that led to a period of stability and eventually the peaceful conquest of Makkah.

q: A Hadith that has a broken chain of narrators is classified as _____.
explanation: Munqati' (broken) refers to a Hadith where one or more narrators are missing from the chain of transmission.

q: The Islamic term for the 'oneness of God' is _____.
explanation: Tawhid is the defining doctrine of Islam's strict monotheism.

q: The 'As-Sab' al-Mathani' mentioned in the Qur'an refers to _____.
explanation: Suratul-Fatihah is referred to as the seven oft-repeated verses because it is mandatory in every rak'ah of prayer.

q: The companion who was the father of Aishah (RA) was _____.
explanation: Abu Bakr As-Siddiq was the Prophet's closest friend and father of his wife Aishah.

q: The 'Hijab' became mandatory for Muslim women in the _____ year after Hijrah.
explanation: Most historical accounts state that the verses regarding Hijab were revealed in the 5th year of AH.

q: The 'Fara'id' refers to _____ in Islam.
explanation: Fara'id (singular: Fard) are the mandatory acts commanded by Allah, such as the Five Pillars.

q: The ruler of Abyssinia who protected the early Muslim migrants was _____.
explanation: The Negus (Najashi) was the Christian King of Abyssinia who provided refuge to Muslims fleeing Makkan persecution.

q: The science of judging the character of Hadith narrators is _____.
explanation: Ilm al-Rijal (Science of Men) involves investigating the biographies and credibility of Hadith narrators.

q: The 'Dower' or Mahr belongs to _____.
explanation: Mahr is the exclusive property of the bride, and neither her husband nor her parents can take it without her consent.

q: The 'Qiblatayn' Mosque is significant because _____.
opts: it is where the Prophet died
it is where the prayer direction changed
it is the first mosque built
explanation: Masjid al-Qiblatayn (Mosque of the Two Qiblahs) is where the revelation came to change the prayer direction from Jerusalem to Makkah.

q: The specific Zakat given before the Eid al-Fitr prayer is _____.
explanation: Zakat al-Fitr is a charitable obligation for every Muslim at the end of Ramadan to ensure the poor can celebrate Eid.

q: The companion who narrated the highest number of Hadiths was _____.
explanation: Abu Hurayrah (RA) spent years in close company with the Prophet specifically to learn and memorize his teachings.
